html:
The king who founded the Akkadian Empire in Mesopotamia and ruled it for more than fifty years, around 2334 to 2279 BCE. His birth date is unknown; the chart shows his reign. He is often called the builder of the first empire.

Later legend says he was a foundling set adrift in a basket on the river, and that he rose to be cupbearer to the king of Kish before seizing power. He built a new capital, Akkad, whose site has never been found. From there he conquered the Sumerian city-states, defeating Lugalzagesi of Uruk, and campaigned into Elam, Syria and Anatolia.

Sargon ruled through governors and a standing army, and boasted that ships from Dilmun and Meluhha docked at Akkad. His Semitic language, Akkadian, became the main written language of the region for two thousand years. He made his daughter Enheduanna high priestess at Ur. His grandson Naram-Sin pushed the empire further, and later kings of Assyria and Babylon looked back on Sargon as their model.
